o1.biggest_strength: Targets Controllers at 50 to 300 person SaaS companies on the pricing-change trigger, keeps every email link-free, and holds non-flagged contacts on a watch list instead of sending them the generic 1.8% opener.
o1.biggest_mistake: Steps 1 and 2 each carry a question plus a separate 'reply yes/steps' offer, which breaks the one-question, one-ask rule, and they promise a one-page summary and 'three steps' that were never supplied.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give each email a single question that is also the ask, drop the invented follow-up assets, and add an opt-out footer.

o2.biggest_strength: Each email is short with exactly one question that is the ask, step 1 opens on the pricing change and the 9-to-4-day proof, and it gives tiered send rules with fallback first lines plus an opt-out footer.
o2.biggest_mistake: It loads all 1,900 contacts, including ones with no pricing trigger, who will get a weaker opener. Step 2's '60 fewer days in close' stretches the arithmetic, and 'last note' edges toward urgency.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Hold untriggered contacts until their pricing page changes, or test them as a separate small cell, and drop the 60-days-a-year framing.

reason: Output 2 follows my copy rules better, with one question and one ask per email, no invented assets, and a compliant footer. Its list rules are also practical, putting pricing-change contacts first and giving the rest a sensible fallback opener, and its expected rates are honest.
